# A New Sensation Emerges on Britain's Got Talent

**LONDON, England (CNN)** — Susan Boyle, meet your successor. Just a week after the Scottish singer captivated the world with her extraordinary audition on "Britain's Got Talent," a 12-year-old Welsh boy with a voice reminiscent of Motown's golden era has captured similar acclaim, earning a standing ovation from the notoriously exacting Simon Cowell for what has been described as a "life-changing" performance.

Shaheen Jafargholi's chances appeared to falter early on when Cowell—known for his lack of patience with mediocrity—cut short his audition after just one verse of "Valerie," the Zutons' song famously reimagined by Amy Winehouse. "You've got this really wrong," Cowell told the young performer. "What do you sing apart from that?"

Undeterred, Jafargholi pivoted to "Who's Loving You," the Smokey Robinson composition made famous by a young Michael Jackson and the Jackson Five. The audience erupted in delight as he delivered a flawless rendition, prompting Cowell and fellow judges Piers Morgan and Amanda Holden to rise to their feet in appreciation. "This is how one song can change your life," Cowell remarked. "This may be the start of something special for you, young man."

**Watch Shaheen Jafargholi's performance on "Britain's Got Talent" »**

Writing on his blog for the show, Morgan singled out Jafargholi as the standout performer of the episode, suggesting he could emerge as a genuine contender to Boyle for the competition's £100,000 ($146,000) grand prize. "Once Simon got him to sing the right kind of song for his voice, he was sensational—like a young Stevie Wonder," Morgan wrote.

In a subsequent interview, Jafargholi revealed that he has been singing since the age of two. "When I was a bit older, my mum got me some singing lessons and my voice just got bigger and bigger," he explained. "Hopefully this is going to be my big break."

Boyle's now-legendary performance last week—delivered by the 47-year-old with a voice worthy of Broadway, who revealed she had never been kissed—propelled the show to international prominence. Her rendition of "I Dreamed a Dream" from *Les Misérables* has since amassed more than 32 million views on YouTube and secured her a series of high-profile American media appearances, including a spot on CNN's *Larry King Live*.

Jafargholi, meanwhile, still has considerable ground to cover to rival Boyle's meteoric rise. As of Monday morning, footage of his performance on YouTube had drawn just 330,000 views.

**Who do you prefer—Susan Boyle or Shaheen Jafargholi? Share your thoughts below.**

# London: A City of Timeless History and Modern Vibrancy

LONDON, England (CNN) — As one of the world's most iconic capital cities, London stands as a testament to centuries of history, culture, and innovation. From the ancient stones of the Tower of London to the gleaming glass towers of Canary Wharf, this sprawling metropolis on the banks of the River Thames continues to captivate millions of visitors and residents alike.

England's capital has long served as a global hub for finance, arts, and politics. The city's skyline tells a story of transformation—Big Ben and the Houses of Parliament stand as enduring symbols of British democracy, while structures like The Shard and 30 St Mary Axe (affectionately known as "The Gherkin") represent London's forward-looking ambitions.

CNN has frequently reported from London, covering everything from royal ceremonies at Buckingham Palace to breaking news in Westminster. The city's role as a media and communications center makes it a natural dateline for international news organizations covering European affairs, British politics, and global economic trends.

Beyond its political and financial significance, London offers an unparalleled cultural landscape. The British Museum houses treasures spanning human civilization, while the West End rivals Broadway as a premier destination for theater enthusiasts. World-class institutions like the Tate Modern and National Gallery showcase artistic masterpieces, and diverse neighborhoods from Camden to Notting Hill reflect the multicultural fabric that defines modern London.

The city's extensive public transportation system, including the iconic London Underground (affectionately called "the Tube"), moves millions of passengers daily, connecting historic boroughs with contemporary business districts.

Whether covering breaking news, royal events, or cultural developments, London remains firmly positioned at the intersection of tradition and modernity—a city where centuries-old customs coexist with cutting-edge innovation, making it perpetually newsworthy on the world stage.
